rationale: Convert part of the snapshot-restore refutation into a measurement. The earlier account relied on raft.restore's stale check and on the log restore setting the committed position; this execution delivers an out-of-date snapshot and a newer one to a follower through its real handler. The predecessor execution of the same scenario completed its deliveries but every comparison returned unknown because the two result events carried no identity field, so no result could be correlated to its admission. The harness now emits the requested snapshot index on both result events, which is fixed by the delivery rather than by the measured outcome, so each result correlates to its own admission. Local construction runs showed the stale snapshot exposed no snapshot and left the commit at 4, while the newer snapshot was exposed at index 10 and advanced the commit to 10. Membership replacement remains source-only and is recorded as such.

scope.description: Snapshot admission at a follower. A follower that has committed index 4 receives an out-of-date snapshot at index 3 and then a newer snapshot at index 10; the snapshot exposed by its update and its committed index are recorded after each delivery.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}, node 1 leads, and node 2 has committed index 4 after the leader's no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both snapshots carry the current voter membership, so the role-map replacement path is a no-op in this case and only the log and commit effects are measured.
The snapshots are delivered as InstallSnapshot messages through the follower's real handler, with indexes 3 and 10 and terms 1 and 2.
Each result event carries the requested snapshot index as its identity field, which is fixed by the delivery and independent of the measured snapshot exposure and commit.
The follower's committed index is read from the harness's tracked commit, which advances only when an update reports a higher commit.
excluded: The case does not exercise membership replacement, the state machine Recover task, or a restart.
No transport or persistence path is exercised.
Snapshot corruption and operator-supplied snapshots are excluded.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, leaving node 2 at committed index 4. It delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 3 to node 2, pumps its update, and records whether a snapshot is exposed and the follower's committed index. It then delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 10, pumps the update, and records the exposed snapshot index and the committed index.
experiment.requirement: A follower must reject a snapshot whose index does not exceed its committed index and must accept a newer one, exposing it for application and advancing its committed index to the snapshot index without moving it backward.
experiment.responsibility: raft.restore owns the index and role guards and delegates to the log restore, which sets the committed and processed positions. The experiment exercises those real paths on a follower and changes only the snapshot index.

comparisons.description: An out-of-date snapshot must not be exposed for application.
The committed index must not move when an out-of-date snapshot is rejected.
The newer snapshot must be exposed at its own index.
Accepting the newer snapshot must advance the committed index to the snapshot index.

experiment.revision_reason: Emit the requested snapshot index on the stale_snapshot_delivered and newer_snapshot_delivered result events so each result carries the identity field declared by its comparison and can be correlated to its own snapshot_delivery_requested admission. The snapshots, delivery order and compared assertions are unchanged from the predecessor.
